name: fix_missing_not_null_constraint
description: Fixes a schema that wrongly allows NULL in orders.customer_id
prompts: The schema in schema.sql defines `customers` and `orders` tables, but the `orders.customer_id` column currently allows NULL values, which lets an order be created with no customer at all - a data integrity bug, since every order must belong to a customer. Fix schema.sql so that `orders.customer_id` can never be NULL, without changing any other column or table.

test_setup_files.test_notnull.py:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
with open('schema.sql', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    conn.executescript(f.read())

conn.execute("INSERT INTO customers (id, name) VALUES (1, 'Alice')")
conn.execute('INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, amount) VALUES (1, 1, 9.99)')
conn.commit()

try:
    conn.execute('INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, amount) VALUES (2, NULL, 5.00)')
    conn.commit()
    raise AssertionError('expected NULL customer_id insert to fail')
except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
    pass

count = conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders').fetchone()[0]
assert count == 1, f'expected only the valid order to be present, got {count}'

print('PASS')
